types.embedding_query_text: Country: A nation-state with defined borders and a government. Also called Nation, State, Country. Examples: France, Belgium, Netherlands.

chosen_type.label: Country
chosen_type.justification: Schema.org's Country class matches the OIE_TYPE definition and mentions (France, Belgium, Netherlands) as sovereign states.

candidates.label: Country
candidates.comment: A Country is a sovereign state or nation, representing a primary administrative division of the Earth's surface. Also called nation, state, sovereign state, realm. Examples: United States, Canada, France, Japan, Brazil.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

candidates.label: NLNonprofitType
candidates.comment: NLNonprofitType is an enumeration for specific non-profit organization types originating from the Netherlands. Also called Dutch non-profit type, Netherlands charity classification. Examples: ANBI (Algemeen Nut Beogende Instelling), SBBI (Sociaal Belang Behartigende Instelling). Distinct from NonprofitType, which is a general enumeration for non-profit types.

candidates.label: Landform
candidates.comment: A Landform is a place representing a natural physical feature of the Earth's surface. Also called geographical feature, terrain feature, natural formation. Examples: mountain, plain, valley, island, river. Distinct from Place, which is a broader category for any location.

candidates.label: GovernmentBenefitsType
candidates.comment: GovernmentBenefitsType is an enumeration of various government benefits, particularly those related to supporting situations like COVID-19. Also called public assistance types, state aid categories, welfare program kinds. Examples: unemployment benefits, stimulus checks, housing assistance, food stamps.

types.embedding_query_text: Event Examples: 2,025 excess deaths, 1,222 excess deaths, 480 excess deaths, 72 drowning deaths.

chosen_type.label: ExcessDeathEvent
chosen_type.definition: An event representing a statistical count of excess deaths or incidents like fires/drownings.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org Event class fits the statistical impact examples (excess deaths, fires). Minting a new event type under Event.

candidates.label: ChildrensEvent
candidates.comment: An event specifically organized and designed for children. Also called kids' event, family event, youth gathering. Examples: A puppet show, a children's birthday party, a school play, a kids' festival.

candidates.label: SportsEvent
candidates.comment: An event involving athletic competition or display. Also called athletic contest, game, match, sporting competition. Examples: a football game, an Olympic event, a marathon race, a tennis tournament.

candidates.label: EducationEvent
candidates.comment: An EducationEvent is an Event focused on learning or instruction. Also called educational activity, learning event, training session. Examples: A university lecture, a workshop on coding, a seminar on financial literacy, a school field trip.

candidates.label: EventSeries
candidates.comment: An EventSeries is an Event representing a collection of events that share unifying characteristics, such as a recurring festival or a thematic lecture series. Also called event cycle, recurring event, series of events. Examples: The Olympic Games, a monthly book club meeting, a season of a concert series, a weekly farmers market.

candidates.label: Error
candidates.comment: An Error is an InstantaneousEvent representing a problem or failure that occurred. Also called fault, malfunction, issue. Examples: A 404 Not Found error, a database connection error, a system crash, a data validation error.

types.embedding_query_text: Time Examples: 22 June to 28 June, 24 June, 2026-07-05 to 2026-07-07, last week of June.

chosen_type.label: Schedule
chosen_type.justification: Schema.org's Schedule class represents recurring time periods, fitting the date ranges in the mentions.

candidates.label: DayOfWeek
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing a specific day of the week, used for scheduling or recurring events. Also called Weekday, calendar day, day name. Examples: Monday, Tuesday, Saturday, Sunday. Distinct from Date, which specifies a particular calendar date.

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: DateTime
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, combining both date and time components according to ISO 8601. Also called Timestamp, date and time string, ISO 8601 datetime. Examples: "2023-10-27T10:30:00Z", "1999-12-31T23:59:59-05:00", "2024-01-15T14:00:00". Distinct from Date, which only specifies a calendar date without time.

candidates.label: CourseInstance
candidates.comment: A CourseInstance is a specific offering of an educational course, distinguished by its particular time, location, medium, or target student group. Also called course section, class session, course offering, specific class. Examples: "Fall 2023 Introduction to Python (Online)," "Spring 2024 Art History 101 (Campus A, Section B)," "Summer Intensive Yoga Teacher Training." Distinct from Course, which is the general description of the educational content.

types.embedding_query_text: GovernmentOfficial: An individual holding a public office in a government. Also called Minister, Official, PublicServant. Examples: Stéphanie Rist, Laurent Nuñez, Sebastien Lecornu.

chosen_type.label: GovernmentOfficial
chosen_type.definition: An individual holding a public office in a governmental organization.
chosen_type.justification: Schema.org lacks a direct class for individuals in government roles; mentions (names) require a Person subclass.

candidates.label: GovernmentOffice
candidates.comment: A GovernmentOffice is a local business representing a specific governmental agency or department. Also called public agency office, state department branch, municipal service center. Examples: IRS office, DMV office, local planning department, social security office. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is the physical structure that may contain multiple offices.

candidates.label: GovernmentService
candidates.comment: A GovernmentService is an intangible service provided by a government organization to the public. Also called public service, state-provided service, municipal offering. Examples: food stamps program, veterans benefits, public education, waste collection.

candidates.label: GovernmentPermit
candidates.comment: A GovernmentPermit is a formal authorization issued by a government agency. Also called public license, state approval, official authorization. Examples: building permit, driver's license, business operating license, fishing permit.

candidates.label: GovernmentOrganization
candidates.comment: A GovernmentOrganization is an organization or agency that is part of a governmental body. Also called public sector entity, state agency, governmental body. Examples: Department of Defense, Environmental Protection Agency, National Institutes of Health, local city council.

candidates.label: PostOffice
candidates.comment: A PostOffice is a GovernmentOffice providing postal services. Also called postal service branch, mail office. Examples: USPS Post Office, Royal Mail sorting office, a local post office branch, a general post office.

chosen_type.label: Temperature
chosen_type.definition: A numerical value combined with a unit of temperature measurement.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class directly represents temperature measurements; mentions require a Quantity subclass.

candidates.label: Energy
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Energy represents a numerical value combined with a unit of energy. Also called power, work, heat. Examples: "100 kWh", "500 Joules", "200 Calories", "1.21 Gigawatts".

candidates.label: WearableMeasurementTypeEnumeration
candidates.comment: An enumeration of common measurement types used for wearable products. Also called wearable sizing type, apparel measurement, garment dimension. Examples: "chest circumference", "sleeve length", "inseam".

candidates.label: AdultOrientedEnumeration
candidates.comment: AdultOrientedEnumeration is an Enumeration of factors that make a product or content relevant or potentially restricted for adults only. Also called adult content classification, age restriction type, mature content indicator. Examples: `AdultSexualContent`, `ViolentContent`, `GamblingContent`.

candidates.label: HowToStep
candidates.comment: A HowToStep is a creative work representing an ordered step in a HowTo guide, which can contain directions and/or tips. Also called instruction stage, procedural step, action sequence. Examples: 'Step 1: Gather Ingredients,' 'Step 2: Preheat Oven,' 'Step 3: Bake for 30 minutes.'

candidates.label: LakeBodyOfWater
candidates.comment: A LakeBodyOfWater is a landform representing a large body of still water surrounded by land. Also called lake, inland sea, reservoir. Examples: Lake Superior, Lake Tahoe, Lake Pontchartrain. Distinct from River, which is flowing water, and OceanBodyOfWater, which is a large saltwater body.

chosen_type.label: Continent
chosen_type.justification: Schema.org's Continent class matches the OIE_TYPE definition and the mention 'Europe'.

candidates.label: Continent
candidates.comment: One of the Earth's large landmasses, such as Europe or Africa. Also called major landmass, global region, land continent. Examples: Asia, North America, Antarctica, Australia. Distinct from Landform, which is a general term for a natural feature of the Earth's surface.

candidates.label: EUEnergyEfficiencyEnumeration
candidates.comment: An EUEnergyEfficiencyEnumeration is an EnergyEfficiencyEnumeration listing the EU energy efficiency classes A-G, A+, A++, and A+++ as defined in EU directive 2017/1369. Also called EU energy rating, European energy class. Examples: EUEnergyEfficiencyCategoryA, EUEnergyEfficiencyCategoryA+++, EUEnergyEfficiencyCategoryG.

candidates.label: TouristDestination
candidates.comment: A place, region, or area that is a primary focus for tourism, often containing multiple tourist attractions. Also called travel destination, vacation spot, tourist region. Examples: Paris, the Grand Canyon, the Caribbean islands, a specific resort town. Distinct from TouristAttraction, which is a specific point of interest within a destination.

candidates.label: Country
candidates.comment: A Country is a sovereign state or nation, representing a primary administrative division of the Earth's surface. Also called nation, state, sovereign state, realm. Examples: United States, Canada, France, Japan, Brazil.

candidates.label: UserPlusOnes
candidates.comment: An outdated type representing a user's interaction of giving a "+1" endorsement, typically on Google+ or similar platforms. Also called user endorsement, +1, social recommendation. Examples: a user giving a +1 to a web page, endorsing a business, recommending content.

chosen_type.label: Percentage
chosen_type.definition: A numerical value expressed as a percentage.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class represents percentages; mentions require a QuantitativeValue subclass.

candidates.label: MerchantReturnEnumeration
candidates.comment: An enumeration of various kinds of product return policies offered by merchants. Also called return policy type, refund option, merchandise return category. Examples: "NoReturns", "FreeReturns", "ReturnsWithFee", "ExchangeOnly".

candidates.label: AdultOrientedEnumeration
candidates.comment: AdultOrientedEnumeration is an Enumeration of factors that make a product or content relevant or potentially restricted for adults only. Also called adult content classification, age restriction type, mature content indicator. Examples: `AdultSexualContent`, `ViolentContent`, `GamblingContent`.

candidates.label: MedicalConditionStage
candidates.comment: A medical intangible representing a specific stage of a medical condition. Also called disease stage, condition phase, severity level. Examples: "Stage IIIa cancer", "early-stage Alzheimer's", "acute phase of an infection".

candidates.label: MonetaryAmountDistribution
candidates.comment: A quantitative value distribution representing a statistical distribution of monetary amounts. Also called money distribution, financial range, income distribution. Examples: "average salary range", "distribution of asset values", "price range for a product category".

candidates.label: DENonprofitType
candidates.comment: DENonprofitType is an enumeration representing specific types of non-profit organizations recognized under German fiscal code, article 52. Also called German non-profit classification, AO 52 non-profit. Examples: A German charitable foundation, a registered German association for public benefit.

types.embedding_query_text: Area Examples: 8,700 hectares, 8,700 ha, 8.7 thousand hectares.

chosen_type.label: AreaMeasurement
chosen_type.definition: A numerical value combined with a unit of area measurement.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class directly represents area measurements; mentions require a QuantitativeValue subclass.

candidates.label: Landform
candidates.comment: A Landform is a place representing a natural physical feature of the Earth's surface. Also called geographical feature, terrain feature, natural formation. Examples: mountain, plain, valley, island, river. Distinct from Place, which is a broader category for any location.

candidates.label: AdministrativeArea
candidates.comment: An AdministrativeArea is a geographical region, typically governed by a specific authority. Also called political division, jurisdiction, governmental region, territory. Examples: A country, a state, a province, a city, a county.

candidates.label: StadiumOrArena
candidates.comment: A large civic structure designed for sporting events, concerts, or other large-scale public gatherings. Also called stadium, arena, coliseum, sports complex. Examples: Wembley Stadium, Madison Square Garden, the Roman Colosseum.

candidates.label: LakeBodyOfWater
candidates.comment: A LakeBodyOfWater is a landform representing a large body of still water surrounded by land. Also called lake, inland sea, reservoir. Examples: Lake Superior, Lake Tahoe, Lake Pontchartrain. Distinct from River, which is flowing water, and OceanBodyOfWater, which is a large saltwater body.

candidates.label: FloorPlan
candidates.comment: A FloorPlan is an Intangible representing an explicit description of a collection of similar accommodations, providing common information like room counts, sizes, and layout diagrams. Also called layout plan, apartment layout, property blueprint. Examples: A floor plan for a two-bedroom apartment, a diagram showing the layout of an office suite, a blueprint for a house model.

types.embedding_query_text: Population Examples: 3,000 people, nearly 3,000 evacuees, 3,000 evacuated individuals.

chosen_type.label: StatisticalPopulation
chosen_type.justification: Schema.org's StatisticalPopulation class fits the example of a count of people in a population.

candidates.label: StatisticalPopulation
candidates.comment: A set of instances of a given type that satisfy specific constraints, used for statistical analysis. Also called statistical group, data population, sample group, target demographic. Examples: all persons with a home location in a specific city, all events occurring in a particular year, all news articles mentioning a certain keyword. Distinct from StatisticalVariable, which represents a measurable metric within a population.

candidates.label: GatedResidenceCommunity
candidates.comment: A GatedResidenceCommunity is a Residence type that is a residential area with restricted access. Also called gated community, private estate. Examples: A luxury residential complex with controlled entry, a retirement community with security gates, a private housing development.

candidates.label: SearchRescueOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization dedicated to finding and providing aid to people who are lost or in imminent danger. Also called SAR team, rescue service, emergency search unit. Examples: a mountain rescue team, a coast guard search and rescue unit, a volunteer SAR group.

candidates.label: City
candidates.comment: A large and permanent human settlement, typically an administrative area with a defined government. Also called town, municipality, urban area, metropolis. Examples: New York City, London, Tokyo, Paris. Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a broader category including states, provinces, etc.

candidates.label: SingleFamilyResidence
candidates.comment: A type of house designed to be occupied by one family, typically detached from other homes. Also called detached house, single-family home, private residence. Examples: a suburban house with a yard, a standalone cottage, a bungalow.

types.embedding_query_text: Location Examples: Sainte-Marie-la-Mer and Canet-en-Roussillon, Iberian Peninsula, Paris, towns in southern France.

candidates.label: TouristDestination
candidates.comment: A place, region, or area that is a primary focus for tourism, often containing multiple tourist attractions. Also called travel destination, vacation spot, tourist region. Examples: Paris, the Grand Canyon, the Caribbean islands, a specific resort town. Distinct from TouristAttraction, which is a specific point of interest within a destination.

candidates.label: TouristAttraction
candidates.comment: A specific place or feature that draws tourists due to its interest or appeal. Also called point of interest, visitor attraction, landmark. Examples: the Eiffel Tower, a national park, a historical museum, a famous statue. Distinct from TouristDestination, which is a broader area containing one or more attractions.

candidates.label: BoatTerminal
candidates.comment: A CivicStructure serving as a station for boats, ships, and other water vessels to dock and embark/disembark passengers or cargo. Also called ferry terminal, cruise port, marina, dock. Examples: "The Seattle Ferry Terminal", "PortMiami cruise terminal", "A local marina office".

candidates.label: LandmarksOrHistoricalBuildings
candidates.comment: LandmarksOrHistoricalBuildings is a place representing an important historical landmark or building. Also called historical site, heritage building, monument. Examples: Eiffel Tower, Colosseum, Statue of Liberty, a historic courthouse.

candidates.label: UserPlusOnes
candidates.comment: An outdated type representing a user's interaction of giving a "+1" endorsement, typically on Google+ or similar platforms. Also called user endorsement, +1, social recommendation. Examples: a user giving a +1 to a web page, endorsing a business, recommending content.

candidates.label: SearchRescueOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization dedicated to finding and providing aid to people who are lost or in imminent danger. Also called SAR team, rescue service, emergency search unit. Examples: a mountain rescue team, a coast guard search and rescue unit, a volunteer SAR group.

candidates.label: Organization
candidates.comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.

candidates.label: Airline
candidates.comment: An Airline is an Organization that provides air transportation services for passengers. Also called air carrier, air transport company, flight operator. Examples: United Airlines, British Airways, Lufthansa, Southwest Airlines. Distinct from Airport, which is the facility where planes take off and land.

candidates.label: ITNonprofitType
candidates.comment: ITNonprofitType is a nonprofit type enumeration specifically for non-profit organizations originating from Italy. Also called Italian non-profit category, Italy NPO type, Italian charity classification. Examples: 'ONLUS', 'APS', 'ODV' (specific Italian non-profit legal forms). Distinct from NonprofitType, which is a more general enumeration of non-profit organization types.

candidates.label: USNonprofitType
candidates.comment: An enumeration of specific non-profit organization types recognized within the United States. Also called US charity type, American non-profit category, US voluntary sector classification. Examples: a 501(c)(3) organization, a public charity, a private foundation.
